author: GamingBolt
description:
Housemarque's Saro is finally available, arriving exactly five years after the original (which is probably a metaphor of some kind). If you've seen the critical response, you'll know it's an amazing game. The problem is whether that's truly enough in this day and age.

Let's be honest: Returnal wasn't exactly a massive hit, reportedly shipping over one million copies in less than a year. Which is fine if Housemarque is independent, but it's now owned by Sony. The same Sony that's more than content to lay off talented studios like Bluepoint when necessary.

This isn't to say that Saros will meet the same fate, especially since it's more approachable and accessible without sacrificing the difficulty that fans know and love. But it was also developed on a bigger budget while retaining many of the same niche gameplay elements. What could happen if it's not a bigger success? Join us as we discuss all this and more.

Update: This is a re-upload of the original video from yesterday. That vid
title: I'm Concerned for Housemarque Despite Saros' Success...

author: GamingBolt
description:
The Blood of Dawnwalker is among the more interesting additions to a very strong line-up of great games in 2026.  Not only is the debut title for a studio composed of many of the folks who made The Witcher 3 such a great game, but it’s shaping up to be a focused, gripping take on vampires that might just set the bar for others looking to bring in creatures of the night into their titles. 

We’ve been obsessing over this one for a while now, and thought it was only right to share important details on it in the wake of the studio opening up pre-orders for the title.
title: The Blood of Dawnwalker - 15 Features You Need To Know Before You Pre-Order

author: GamingBolt
description:
It isn’t everyday you see us, or anybody else for that matter, revisit a review of a game. It’s even rare to see that second review pop up a mere month after its release. But that’s what the developer has managed to do with Crimson Desert, changing enough about how it feels to play that it could be seen as a far cry from what Pywel was when the game released to a rather muted reception thanks to its flaws.

Those flaws have been meaningfully fixed now, and they’ve been addressed so well that we decided to give this one the Cyberpunk treatment. Why did we decide that, and how? That’s what we’re here to examine. Join us as we take you through why we felt Crimson Desert deserved a second review, and what made us bump up its score from what we originally rated it for.

title: Why Did We Re-Review Crimson Desert So Soon After Launch?
